texts: When retrograde cardioplegia gives a low line pressure and the heart does not arrest, the most likely reason is a persistent left superior vena cava.
A left SVC drains into the coronary sinus and enlarges it, so solution given into the sinus runs out up the left SVC instead of perfusing the heart.
The left SVC can be snared briefly during retrograde delivery if a bridging vein is present, or antegrade cardioplegia relied on.
A leaking clamp or hidden coronary disease does not cause a low retrograde line pressure, and a cannula pushed too far into the sinus usually gives a high pressure, not a low one.
In the picture, the banana water fountains out of the second chimney on the left, the hose hangs slack and the fans keep spinning.
Memory hook: a slack hose and a fountain on the left: the second chimney.
